JUDY GRACI'S NOTICE OF SUPPORT FOR
KENNEDY AND BURROW'S REQUEST FOR INDEPENDENT
INVESTIGATION AND FORENSIC AUDIT
TO THE HONORABLE COMMISSION AND ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
Judy Graci, pro se intervenor in Docket No. 59475, respectfully files this Notice of Support for the “Response to Remand – Request for Independent Investigation and Forensic Audit” filed by Kevin Kennedy and John Burrow on September 17, 2026 (the “Kennedy-Burrow Request”), and in support states as follows:
1. Nature of this Notice
Judy Graci joins in and supports the Kennedy-Burrow Request in its entirety and respectfully urges the Commission to grant the relief requested therein. This is a short notice of support rather than a restatement of the full record; Ms. Graci incorporates the Kennedy-Burrow Request by reference.
2. Grounds for Support
Ms. Graci supports the Kennedy-Burrow Request for the following principal reasons, each of which is more fully addressed in that filing:
a. ERCOT appears to have developed two materially different 2024 system-wide models – the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (“PBRP”) and the 2024 Regional Transmission Plan (“2024-RTP”) – using inconsistent temporal and spatial load and generation assumptions, despite being developed contemporaneously from the same available data.
b. Those inconsistencies raise legitimate, unresolved questions as to whether the PBRP's modeling complied with NERC Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1 (Requirements R1, R2, and R3) and NERC Standards MOD-032 and MOD-033, which govern the data quality, consistency, and validation required of planning models.
c. The three approved 765-kV import paths total approximately 1,255 miles, are projected to cost approximately $11 billion, and will require eminent domain authority over thousands of Texas landowners and tens of thousands of acres of private property – including generational family land – making independent verification of the underlying modeling a matter of substantial public interest.
d. A reasonable, testable question exists as to whether ERCOT's subsequent 2024-RTP analysis independently established the need for the PBRP 765-kV import paths or simply incorporated those paths into its starting topology as assumed, already-justified facilities.
e. The Kennedy-Burrow Request does not allege wrongdoing by ERCOT and expressly disclaims any such accusation; it asks only that the Commission obtain an independent, technical determination of whether the modeling underlying an $11 billion infrastructure commitment is sound before that commitment becomes irreversible.
3. Relief Requested
Ms. Graci respectfully requests that the Commission grant the relief set forth in Section XIV of the Kennedy-Burrow Request, including, without limitation: (a) opening a formal investigation into the modeling underlying the PBRP; (b) directing an independent forensic and technical audit of the PBRP and the contemporaneous 2024-RTP models, including bus-level reconciliation of load and generation assumptions and NERC TPL-001-5.1, MOD-032, and MOD-033 compliance review; (c) abating further action on the three PBRP 765-kV import paths pending completion, public release, and legislative review of that audit; and (d) any other relief the Commission deems appropriate.
4. Conclusion
For the foregoing reasons, Ms. Graci respectfully requests that the Commission grant the Kennedy-Burrow Request and order the independent investigation and forensic audit described therein.
Respectfully submitted,
